evals.prompt: I have a Freezed DTO that also uses json_serializable. My generated code has errors about undefined symbols. What's the correct way to write the part directives?
evals.expected_output: The freezed part must come BEFORE the .g.dart part. Correct order: part 'user_dto.freezed.dart'; then part 'user_dto.g.dart'; — reversed order causes undefined symbol errors. Also needs fromJson factory.

assertions.text: Response explicitly states the .freezed.dart part directive must come BEFORE the .g.dart part directive
Response shows the correct order: freezed first, then .g.dart
Response mentions the fromJson factory constructor is required when using @JsonSerializable on a @freezed class

evals.prompt: After upgrading to Freezed 3.x, my build_runner is failing with an error about my state class. What changed in Freezed 3.x that could cause this?
evals.expected_output: Freezed 3.x requires classes to be abstract, sealed, or manually implement _$MyClass. Plain class MyState with _$MyState no longer works. For union types/BLoC states, use sealed class. For DTOs, use abstract class. Shows corrected code.

assertions.text: Response identifies that Freezed 3.x requires classes to be abstract, sealed, or implement _$MyClass — plain class is no longer allowed
Response recommends sealed class for union types (BLoC states, events) — enables exhaustive switch without default
Response recommends abstract class for DTOs and simple immutable value objects

evals.prompt: Should I add *.g.dart and *.freezed.dart to .gitignore so the generated files aren't committed to the repo?
evals.expected_output: NO — generated files should be committed. CI does NOT run build_runner. The CI workflow verifies generated files are up-to-date (git diff --exit-code on *.g.dart). Adding them to .gitignore breaks CI because the generated files won't be present.

assertions.text: Response says NOT to add generated files to .gitignore — they should be committed
Response explains that CI does not run build_runner — it verifies committed generated files are up-to-date
